explanation:
The `timer_settime()` and `timer_gettime()` system calls manage the state of a POSIX per-process timer previously created using `timer_create(2)`. These functions are part of the POSIX Real-time Extensions.

`timer_settime()` is used to arm (start), disarm (stop), or change the expiration parameters of the timer specified by `timerid`. The new settings are provided via the `new_value` argument, which points to an `itimerspec` structure. This structure contains two `timespec` sub-structures: `it_value` (the initial time until the timer expires) and `it_interval` (the subsequent reload interval for a periodic timer).

If `new_value->it_value` is nonzero, the timer is armed and will first expire after the specified time. If `new_value->it_value` is zero (both seconds and nanoseconds fields are zero), the timer is immediately disarmed.

If the optional `old_value` argument is provided (non-NULL), the system stores the timer's previous setting (the time remaining until the next expiration and the previous interval) into the structure it points to.

`timer_gettime()` retrieves the current status of the timer identified by `timerid`. The time remaining until the next expiration (in `it_value`) and the reload interval (in `it_interval`) are stored in the structure pointed to by `curr_value`.

Both functions return 0 on success and -1 on failure, setting `errno`. Common errors include `EINVAL` (the requested time value or interval is invalid or negative), and `EFAULT` (one of the pointer arguments references an inaccessible memory location). These functions require linking against the real-time library (`-lrt`).
keywords: timer_settime, timer_gettime, POSIX timer, real-time, itimerspec, timespec, timer_create, arm timer, disarm timer, -lrt
example_explanation: This C code example creates a POSIX timer, arms it using `timer_settime()` to expire in 3 seconds and repeat every 1 second, and immediately verifies the settings using `timer_gettime()`. After waiting, it disarms the timer by calling `timer_settime()` with a zero `it_value`.
